About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role:

The Safeguards ML Sampling Path team builds and operates the production services that power Claude's safety systems. These services sit on the token generation path across every platform Claude runs on: every request must pass through them, and each millisecond of added latency is wait time for our users. You’ll keep p99 latency flat as traffic grows, build for robustness as dependencies time out or partially fail, and ship changes safely to a system that cannot go down.

What you'll do:

• Design, build, and operate the backend systems that process every token on the generation path for Claude requests, including the streaming contract with the API and inference engines.
• Own latency and reliability end to end: define and maintain SLOs and error budgets for added latency, time-to-first-token, and availability, and lead incident response and postmortem follow-through.
• Ship changes to the hot path rapidly but safely — canaried and gradual rollouts, error budget and latency gating, fast rollbacks — and drive per-token performance: chase tail latency and keep cost flat as traffic, models, and checks per request grow.
• Set technical direction for the sampling path: lead design reviews, make latency, reliability, and cost trade-off calls with the inference and research teams, mentor engineers, and raise the operational bar for the wider Safeguards organization.

You may be a good fit if you:

• Have designed, built, and operated high QPS systems at global scale, and were accountable for them in production: incident response, outages, and postmortem-driven remediation.
• Have a strong foundation in distributed systems: replication, consistency tradeoffs, failure modes, and SLO management under load.
• Design systems for graceful degradation: you plan for a slow dependency, a dropped stream, or a half-rolled-out deploy before it happens, and build so the system degrades predictably instead of failing.
• Have successfully shipped broad or all-encompassing changes to mission critical systems (e.g., database migrations, interface changes, rewrites).

Strong candidates may also have:

• 8+ years of industry software engineering experience.
• Familiarity with LLM inference systems and transformer-based models (not required, but a plus).

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$320,000—$485,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As a Channel Partner Manager for Korea, you will be responsible for building, managing, and scaling strategic partnerships with both System Integrators (SIs) and resellers to accelerate the adoption of our solutions in the Korean market. You will work at the intersection of cutting-edge technology and Korea's unique business ecosystem, helping partners integrate our products into their solution portfolios and joint go-to-market strategies.

As a Channel Partner Manager, you will focus on growing the partner Anthropic reseller and services business in Korea and achieving quarterly revenue and partner attach targets through new customers and upsells. You'll be the local owner of these partner relationships in Korea. Our partners will look to you for everything that makes the channel work day to day from initial onboarding to deal registration, enablement, billing and contracting questions, escalations. Our internal teams will look to you for what is happening in the market, how partners are driving new opportunities and growth within existing customers. You'll work closely with the local sales team and the central program team, co-selling on partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities and managing direct versus partner conflict as deals arise. Strong business creation skills are needed to identify joint value propositions and explore co-selling models. Much of the process for running the channel in Korea doesn't exist yet, and building it will be a large part of the job in the first year. While revenue contribution is the key metric, building scalable partner engagement and executing joint initiatives are crucial for consistent growth.

This is an early role in a new market for a program we expect to grow well beyond its first two countries. The habits you establish with our first partners in Korea will shape how the program works everywhere else.

Key responsibilities

• Own the day-to-day relationships with Anthropic's strategic resellers and system integrators in Korea, acting as their primary local point of contact, including billing, contracting and general queries
• Own deal registration and pipeline discipline with partners, making sure registrations are submitted and validated, conflicts are cleared, and named end-customer reporting is complete on every deal
• Forecast and report partner pipeline and performance against the quarterly revenue and partner attach targets, and own the Korea channel number with the central program team
• Negotiate resale agreements and commercial terms with partners alongside the central program team and Legal
• Co-sell with the local account team on partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities, and manage direct versus partner conflict as deals arise
• Develop and execute business plans with System Integrators and strategic resellers to drive mutual growth and revenue targets
• Build and maintain executive-level relationships within Korean partner organizations, navigating complex organizational structures and decision-making processes
• Support partner onboarding end to end, from diligence and agreement execution through readiness ahead of launch, including for partners who join the program after launch
• Coordinate partner certification and enablement with the central enablement lead, including Korean-language delivery and ongoing recertification
• Manage Anthropic's counterpart relationships with the cloud hyperscalers AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure in Korea, including the Marketplace private offer motion that reseller deals run through
• Work with the central program team on program governance, margin mechanics, and escalations, and build the local processes and working rhythms the channel needs where none exist yet, feeding what you learn from partners back to the program team
• Run regular business reviews and QBRs with each partner against the joint plan
• Own partner co-marketing in Korea, agreeing a joint marketing plan with each partner and Channel Marketing, funding it through MDF where it qualifies, and delivering the announcements, campaigns, webinars and events that turn the partnership into pipeline

Minimum qualifications

• Experience managing channel or reseller partner relationships in enterprise software or cloud
• Experience working with large Korean systems integrators or cloud managed service providers, and an understanding of how partner-led selling works in Korean enterprise, public sector, and financial services accounts
• Working knowledge of channel program mechanics such as deal registration and partner tiering
• Full professional fluency in Korean and professional working proficiency in English, written and spoken, including the ability to deliver enablement to partners in Korean
• Comfort joining a new program early: hands-on, structured, and able to build process where none exists yet
• Are excited about Anthropic's mission to develop AI that is safe and beneficial

Preferred qualifications

• Experience with cloud marketplace resale, particularly AWS Marketplace private offers, or with AWS partner teams more generally
• Familiarity with margin and rebate mechanics in a partner program
• Experience bringing existing, informal partner activity into a structured program, or joining a partner program at or before launch
• Experience on the systems integrator or managed service provider side of a vendor relationship, as well as the vendor side
• Familiarity with how enterprises and public sector organizations in Korea are evaluating and adopting AI

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Overview

Permanent, full-time

Please submit your CV in English.

Connecting clients to markets – and talent to opportunity.

With 5,400+ employees and over 80,000 institutional, commercial, and payments clients, we operate from more than 80 offices spread across six continents. As a Fortune 100, Nasdaq-listed provider, we connect clients to the global markets – focusing on innovation, human connection, and providing world-class products and services to all types of investors. Whether you want to forge a career connecting our retail clients to potential trading opportunities, or ingrain yourself in the world of institutional investing, StoneX Group is made up of four business segments that offer endless potential for progression and growth

Business Segment Overview: Engage in a deep variety of business-critical activities that keep our company running efficiently. From strategic marketing and financial management to human resources and operational oversight, you’ll have the opportunity to optimize processes and implement game-changing policies.

Responsibilities

Job Purpose:

We are seeking an experienced Software Application Support Engineer and Level 3 Engineer to join our Payments Technology team. This role is suited for a hands-on engineer who can develop and enhance mission-critical payment applications, provide deep technical ownership for complex production issues, and drive continuous improvement through automation, cloud engineering, and AI-enabled solutions. The successful candidate will work across application development, L3 incident/problem resolution, platform reliability, and intelligent automation to help build scalable, resilient, and future-ready payment platforms.

Primary duties will include:

Application Development & Engineering:

• Design, develop, enhance, and maintain enterprise-grade payment applications using Java/.NET and modern engineering practices.
• Build and support APIs, integrations, and application services that enable secure and reliable payment processing.
• Participate across the software development lifecycle including requirement analysis, solution design, coding, testing, release support, and post-implementation validation.
• Collaborate with architects, product owners, business stakeholders, and support teams to deliver scalable, resilient, and maintainable technology solutions.

Level 3 Problem Resolution:

• Provide Level 3 technical ownership for complex issues across payment applications, databases, integrations, APIs, and cloud-hosted services.
• Lead deep-dive troubleshooting, root cause analysis, defect identification, and permanent fix implementation for recurring or high-impact incidents.
• Work closely with development and operations teams to resolve code-level, configuration, performance, and data-related issues.
• Support major incident restoration activities while ensuring long-term corrective actions are delivered through engineering improvements.

AI Development & Intelligent Automation:

• Identify, design, and develop AI-enabled solutions that improve application support, incident analysis, operational efficiency, and knowledge discovery.
• Contribute to Generative AI and Agentic AI use cases such as support assistants, automated RCA summaries, log analysis, alert correlation, and intelligent ticket triage.
• Use AI tools and frameworks to accelerate development, improve code quality, enhance documentation, and reduce manual support effort.
• Partner with technology teams to embed AI-driven insights and automation into payment application support and engineering workflows.

Cloud Engineering & Platform Reliability:

• Support, enhance, and troubleshoot applications hosted on Azure and related cloud platforms.
• Work with cloud-native services, containers, Kubernetes, monitoring, logging, and deployment automation to improve reliability and operational readiness.
• Contribute to performance tuning, resilience improvements, security compliance, disaster recovery readiness, and cloud cost optimization.

DevOps, Automation & Continuous Improvement:

• Develop automation scripts and tools using Python, PowerShell, or similar technologies to reduce manual effort and improve response times.
• Support CI/CD pipelines, release validation, environment automation, and deployment governance for payment applications.
• Drive shift-left improvements by converting recurring support issues into permanent engineering fixes, automation, monitoring enhancements, or knowledge articles.

ITIL Process Adherence:

• Ensure compliance with ITIL processes, particularly Incident Management and Problem Management, to ensure service continuity and minimize downtime.
• Contribute to the implementation and improvement of ITIL best practices within the organization.

Documentation & Reporting:

• Maintain accurate records of incidents, problems, changes, and resolutions.
• Generate and analyze reports on service performance, identifying trends and opportunities for improvement.

Qualifications

To land this role you will need:

• Strong hands-on experience in application development using Java or .NET, with the ability to understand, debug, enhance, and support enterprise applications.
• Experience supporting mission-critical applications at Level 3, including code-level troubleshooting, RCA, defect resolution, and production stability improvements.
• Working knowledge of payment applications, APIs, integrations, transaction processing, or financial services technology would be highly valuable.
• Database experience with MongoDB and SQL, including query analysis, stored procedures, performance troubleshooting, and data issue investigation.
• Hands-on experience with Azure or other major cloud platforms, including application hosting, monitoring, security, and infrastructure troubleshooting.
• Experience with automation and scripting using Python, PowerShell, or similar tools.
• Understanding of DevOps, CI/CD, observability, logging, monitoring, and incident tracking tools.
• Good understanding of ITIL practices, particularly Incident Management, Problem Management, Change Management, and Knowledge Management.
• Exposure to AI, Generative AI, Agentic AI, Azure AI Services, OpenAI, AI-assisted development, prompt engineering, or intelligent automation use cases.

What will make you stand out:

• Experience building AI-powered tools, support assistants, knowledge bots, or automation workflows for application support and engineering teams.
• Experience with payment platforms, SWIFT, ISO 20022, transaction monitoring, reconciliation, or financial messaging systems.
• Hands-on exposure to Kubernetes, Rancher, ServiceNow, Azure monitoring, or enterprise observability platforms.
• Ability to convert recurring production issues into engineering backlog items, automation opportunities, or platform reliability improvements.
• Strong ownership mindset with the ability to work across development, operations, architecture, business, and global support teams.

Certifications (Good To Have):

• ITIL certification (ITIL Foundation or higher).

DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. We explore robotics and automation to transform last-mile logistics in the long term. If you have a passion for applying robotics solutions in a service used by millions of people, then we want to talk to you!

About the Role

You will be a fundamental and experienced member of the Service Operations team at DoorDash Labs. You will complete more advanced diagnostic and repair work to maximize uptime, supporting our overall fleet utilization goals. You will report to the Associate Operations Manager, Service, in our DoorDash Labs organization. This is an on-site role with expectations of 100% in-office in Fremont, CA, San Jose, CA, or Sunnyvale, CA.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

• Execute any Senior Service Technician task and:
• Diagnose complex, intermittent, or unusual faults in robotic systems, modular components, and support vehicles, often requiring advanced troubleshooting techniques and interpretation of complex data
• Perform advanced repairs, including component-level troubleshooting and fixes on intricate electrical systems, control units, and associated hardware, with minimal supervision
• Interpret complex technical manuals, schematics, and diagnostic flowcharts to guide troubleshooting efforts
• Meticulously document complex diagnostic processes, root cause hypotheses, non-standard troubleshooting steps, repair details, and component failure information in the service management system, contributing potential updates to the knowledge base
• Provide technical guidance, mentorship, and on-the-job assistance to Level 2 Technicians for challenging tasks

We operate 7 days a week, 16 hrs a day to support Robot Operations. During training, you will be on a temporary schedule until your on-the-job training is completed over a few weeks. Once training is complete in Fremont, CA, you will move to your permanent shift assignment that will be based on business need, either an AM or PM shift with weekend coverage. To ensure you can plan accordingly, permanent shift reassignments are provided with at least two weeks' notice.

We’re excited about you because you have…

• 2+ years of service work experience
• Curiosity and an inclination for all things mechanical and repair
• Strong communication and documentation skills
• Prior experience in vehicle or fleet service (especially for electric or autonomous vehicles), robotics, or aircraft is a major plus
• Experience with JIRA, MaintainX, and other service tools and systems is a major plus
• Valid U.S. drivers license required and a successful completion of MVR required

Compensation

Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location.

Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. About the Role

Cursor is the AI code editor used by software engineers across the federal government and the contractors who support them. We are now building a dedicated motion into the civilian Cabinet-level agency ecosystem — DHS, DOJ, DOE, Treasury, HHS, State, and the dozens of bureaus and offices within them that run significant software development operations.

This role owns SpaceXAI's civilian government channel: building relationships with the prime contractors, systems integrators, and federal consulting firms that develop and operate software for Cabinet-level civilian agencies. The mission is to embed Cursor into the software development workflows of every engineer building for the federal civilian government.

Civilian agencies run some of the most complex software in the world — border management at CBP, financial systems at Treasury, scientific computing at DOE national labs, law enforcement infrastructure at FBI. The developers inside those programs need better tools, and Cursor is already being used by individuals inside these agencies. This role builds the formal channel motion to make it the standard.

This is a senior individual contributor role with revenue ownership, reporting directly to sales leadership.

What You'll Do

Prime contractor and channel partnerships

- Own and grow SpaceXAI's relationships with prime contractors and systems integrators focused on civilian agency programs: Accenture Federal Services, Deloitte Government and Public Services (GPS), Booz Allen Hamilton (Civil division), Leidos Civil, SAIC, CACI, Maximus Federal, Guidehouse, ICF, and contractors supporting MITRE-operated FFRDC programs

- Negotiate and close partnership agreements — reseller arrangements, teaming agreements, and approved vendor designations — that embed Cursor into software delivery workflows on civilian agency programs

- Work with prime BD and program management teams to co-sell Cursor into new civilian agency contract awards at the proposal stage

- Identify and develop relationships with federal consulting firms and boutique civilian-agency integrators that can serve as channel partners or pull-through vehicles

Agency end-user pull-through

- Build relationships inside DHS (CBP, USCIS, ICE, TSA, CISA, FEMA, Coast Guard), DOJ (FBI, DEA, ATF, USMS), DOE (NNSA, national laboratory network including Sandia, Los Alamos, Lawrence Livermore, PNNL, Argonne, Oak Ridge), and other Cabinet-level agencies at the IT, software engineering, and digital transformation leadership level

- Engage agency CIOs, CDOs, and digital service offices to build awareness and preference for Cursor within civilian agency software development standards and procurement pipelines

- Develop relationships with the US Digital Service (USDS), GSA (18F, Login.gov http://Login.gov, cloud.gov http://cloud.gov), and agency-embedded digital transformation teams that influence tooling standards across the civilian government

- Represent SpaceXAI at ACT-IAC events, AFCEA Federal, agency industry days, and civilian government technology conferences; establish SpaceXAI's presence in the federal civilian IT community

Revenue and pipeline

- Own a revenue target for civilian government channel business

- Build and manage a pipeline of prime contractor partnerships and program-level co-sell opportunities across civilian agency programs

- Forecast and report on channel pipeline with the same rigor as direct enterprise deals

- Identify and pursue contract vehicles relevant to civilian software tools: GSA IT Schedule 70, CIO-SP4, Alliant 2/3, and agency-specific BPAs and IDIQs

Cross-functional

- Work with SpaceXAI's legal and compliance teams on teaming agreements, vendor qualification, and FedRAMP authorization planning — civilian agencies are more likely to require FedRAMP than DoD, and this candidate should be able to navigate those conversations honestly and strategically

- Partner with Field Engineering on technical evaluations and POCs inside prime contractor and agency developer environments

- Channel civilian agency developer feedback and product requirements back to SpaceXAI's roadmap team — DOE national labs in particular will push requirements for high-performance computing, scientific workflows, and air-gapped environments that no other customer segment will surface

What We're Looking For

Required

- Active Secret clearance — non-negotiable; candidates without an active Secret clearance will not be considered

- US Citizenship required

- 5+ years of channel sales, BD, or partnership management experience inside the federal civilian government market, with direct exposure to Cabinet-level agency programs

- Existing relationships at one or more prime contractors or systems integrators active in the civilian agency market at the BD, program management, or technical leadership level

- Understanding of civilian government procurement mechanics: GSA Schedule 70, IDIQ vehicles (CIO-SP4, Alliant 2/3), agency-specific BPAs, and the role of FedRAMP in civilian agency software procurement

- Track record of standing up or expanding channel/partner relationships that drove material software or technology revenue ($500K+) in the civilian federal market

- Comfortable navigating both the prime-facing channel layer (BD, program managers, contracting) and the end-user pull-through layer (agency software engineers, IT leads, digital transformation offices)

Strong plus

- Active TS/SCI or DOE Q clearance

- Prior experience or service at a Cabinet-level civilian agency in a software, IT, data, or digital transformation role

- Experience selling developer tools, AI/ML platforms, or SDLC tooling through or alongside civilian federal prime contractors

- Existing relationships at DHS (any component), DOJ (FBI, DEA, or USMS), DOE (NNSA or national laboratory), or Treasury/HHS digital service offices

- Familiarity with FedRAMP authorization processes and the ability to position a pre-authorization vendor's roadmap credibly in front of civilian agency procurement teams

- Network within the civilian federal prime ecosystem: Accenture Federal Services, Deloitte GPS, Booz Allen Civil, Leidos Civil, SAIC Civil

- Understanding of DOE national laboratory culture and procurement — national labs operate outside standard civilian agency procurement in meaningful ways and represent some of the largest software development communities in the federal government

Why this role

Cabinet-level civilian agencies employ tens of thousands of software developers and spend billions on technology contracts annually. Cursor is already being used by engineers inside these agencies and the contractors that support them. The formal channel motion does not yet exist. This role builds it from scratch, with a product developers choose independently, a growing prime contractor presence to build on, and direct access to SpaceXAI's GTM and product leadership.

About the Company:

NetEase, Inc. (Nasdaq: NTES and HKEX: 9999) is a global powerhouse in the Internet and video game industry, with a market capitalization of $70+ billion and more than 25,000 employees worldwide. The NetEase group encompasses a range of innovative businesses centered around content creation, including:

• NetEase Games, one of the largest and most renowned game developers worldwide by size, revenue and game offerings. Over the years, NetEase Games has focused on developing high quality content and providing the best experience for gamers around the world;
• Youdao (NYSE: DAO), a majority-controlled subsidiary of NetEase, Inc. and China’s leading technology-focused intelligent learning company;
• Cloud Music (HKEX: 9899), a majority-controlled subsidiary of NetEase, Inc. and China’s leading online music content community;
• Yanxuan, NetEase’s private label consumer lifestyle brand; and
• Other innovative businesses, including, among others, an online payment platform and to-B technology solutions.

About this Role:

This is your chance to have a critical impact at a dynamic gaming company in the midst of an exciting globalization journey. You'll be joining the Group International Legal Department which oversees legal matters for the NetEase group and coordinates with the legal teams within each division of the group.

We are looking for a talented Group Transactional and Commercial Counsel. In this leadership role, you will be advising on a dynamic range of M&A, investments and divestments across multiple jurisdictions, and technology, media and telecom and general commercial matters at the highest international standards, including licensing, outsourcing, software technology development and professional services agreements, innovative FinTech projects, regulatory matters and cross-border technology transfers.

This position will report to the General Counsel of NetEase, Inc.

NetEase operates in multiple countries globally, and this role is primarily responsible for:

Corporate Transactions

• Lead deal execution on a wide range of corporate transactions, including structuring, drafting, and negotiating transaction documents for acquisitions, disposals, minority investments, fund investments, financing transactions and joint ventures across multiple jurisdictions.
• Assess and advise senior stakeholders on legal, regulatory, and commercial risks relating to corporate transactions.
• Navigate regulatory approvals including antitrust, foreign investment clearances, and securities law requirements across multiple jurisdictions.
• Work with legal team to provide end-to-end transaction support, including structuring, due diligence, drafting, negotiation, and completion.
• Coordinate closely with internal business teams (e.g., senior management of business units and the NetEase group, business development, finance, tax, etc.) on all aspects of transactions.
• Provide legal support on post-transaction monitoring and corporate governance matters.

Commercial Contract Management & TMT Advisory

• Draft, review, and negotiate a variety of TMT and other commercial agreements for the NetEase group and individual business units across multiple jurisdictions.
• Provide thought leadership regarding the legal and regulatory aspects of projects involving cutting-edge technologies such as Web3, blockchain, AI, tokenization, online payment systems, AI, etc.
• Advise on TMT related policies and procedures, including terms of use and custody and trust arrangements.
• Keep up-to-date with the most recent technology legal and business developments and continue to develop relevant knowledge within the sectors in which the NetEase group operates.
• Support NetEase group's corporate functions (finance, tax, procurement, IT, corporate secretarial, corporate M&A/ JV, global investments, HR, treasury and others), including daily contract reviews, in-house advisory and commercial disputes.
• Establish contract standards and templates to streamline the review process for everyday commercial agreements across business units.

Core Competencies

• Lead and mentor a high-performing team of legal counsel, fostering a collaborative, business-oriented legal culture, and work closely with other legal specialists within the NetEase group.
• Provide training to the wider legal & internal control functions, business partners and executive leadership.
• Select, manage and coordinate external counsel and advisors across different jurisdictions to ensure high-quality, cost-effective representation.
• Ability to bridge international deals using high-level Mandarin and English language skills to review and negotiate bilingual transaction and commercial documents.

Qualifications:

• Admitted and licensed attorney in U.S., Hong Kong, Singapore or another major common-law jurisdiction with 8+ years relevant post-qualification experience working in well-regarded law firms and/or in-house legal teams; in-house experience preferred.
• Ability to lead, manage and motivate team members located in multiple jurisdictions.
• Self-starter and able to navigate various stakeholders/ businesses operating in different sectors and jurisdictions.
• Excellent transactional training.
• Expertise with TMT laws, regulations and industry best practices across different regions, including an understanding of emerging trends such as in the areas of FinTech/blockchain, money transmission, AI, online game regulation and digital infrastructure.
• Strong drafting, negotiating and problem-solving skills and the ability to manage complex issues and deal structures.
• Excellent leadership and communication skills, with the flexibility and cultural sensitivity to bring different perspectives together and work through competing priorities.
• Demonstrated leadership abilities, including the ability to influence and drive change within the organization.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make informed decisions in complex situations.
• Experienced in managing outside counsel.
• Comfortable working with a geographically dispersed team.
• High-level proficiency in Mandarin Chinese and English is a must.
• Preferred Location: Hong Kong, Singapore or another Asia-Pacific hub; U.S., Canada or other locations considered for exceptional candidates.

Fair Employment Practices
At NetEase, we are committed to fair employment practices. We welcome applications from all individuals, irrespective of age, gender, race, religion, marital status and family responsibilities, or disability.
